paper.title_en: Linear Codes Over Finite Fields From Lattice Polytopes: Structure, Duality, and Quantum Constructions
paper.abstract_en: Linear codes constructed from combinatorial and geometric structures have played a central role in both classical and quantum coding theory. In this paper, we discuss a class of linear codes over finite fields, called polytope codes, obtained via defining sets derived from lattice polytopes. Unlike evaluation-based constructions, our approach exploits the intersection structure of polytope faces to directly control the algebraic and metric properties of the resulting codes. We develop a general defining-set framework for polytope codes and explicitly determine their lengths, dimensions, minimum distances, and Hamming weight distributions. This leads to infinite families of projective, few-weight, distance-optimal, and almost distance-optimal codes. Sufficient conditions for minimality are derived, resulting in new minimal codes that are well suited for applications to secret-sharing schemes. We further study the duals and hulls of polytope codes and provide explicit characterizations of self-orthogonal and linear complementary dual (LCD) families. One of the central results of the paper is a complete classification of quantum codes arising from polytope codes via the Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) construction. We show that the geometry of face intersections fully determines whether the resulting quantum code is a standard CSS code, an LCD-based code, or an entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting code, and we explicitly compute the required entanglement in the latter case. As a consequence, new families of binary, ternary, and prime-power quantum codes with previously unattained parameters are obtained. The proposed polytope-based framework unifies classical and quantum code constructions under a common geometric principle and opens new avenues for applications in cryptography, distributed storage, and quantum information processing. Mathematics Subject Classification. 94B05, 52B20, 11T71, 94A62, 94A45.
